messages:
jia: Quick bring-up — ran a smoke suite for a new spectral-subspace embedding (spectra-v2) on wiki100k + short-query holdout. Posting the short numbers so we can decide if it’s worth a full run.

jia: Summary (small table):
```
model: spectra-v2
float32 recall@1/5/10: 0.728 / 0.842 / 0.887
int8 (per-tensor) recall@1/5/10: 0.673 / 0.805 / 0.858
int8 (per-channel) recall@1/5/10: 0.716 / 0.834 / 0.882
silhouette (kmeans, 50clusters): float32 0.42 -> int8(pt) 0.33 -> int8(pc) 0.40
```

jia: Notes — int8 per-tensor shows an obvious recall hit and cluster collapse in UMAP; per-channel mostly recovers. Latency reductions look good (tokens/sec roughly +28% on p4d for int8).

sam: Nice — what quant tool/config did you use? Was this dynamic or calibration-based?

jia: Used our standard post-training quant flow (calib on wiki1000 subset, symmetric, per-tensor default). Per-channel was done via `--quant per_channel` with 512-bin KL calibration.

sam: Can you paste the exact eval command?

jia: Sure: 
```
./runtest embeddings \
  --model spectra-v2 \
  --dataset s3://redwood-evals/wiki100k/shortholdout.jsonl \
  --quant per_channel \
  --k 10 \
  --index faiss_ivf_flat \
  --batch 1024
```

karen: Quick thought — try calibration with the short-query distribution instead of wiki1000 (our failure mode often comes from mismatch). Also test whitening + L2-norm before index.

emily: Do you have NN examples where it fails? Example queries show semantic drift vs float?

jia: Yep, posted two quick examples (id: 3421 / 3422):
- Query(id=3421): "best way to migrate postgres to aurora"
  - float32 top1: doc_128 (good), int8(pt) top1: doc_999 (bad), int8(pc) top1: doc_128 (good)
- Query(id=3422): "oauth token refresh loop"
  - float32 top1: doc_88, int8(pt) top1: doc_421, int8(pc) top1: doc_88

ben: Seems like per-tensor scale mismatch collapses some subspace directions. Can we try per-channel + symmetric vs asymmetric scale? Also try FP16 baseline to check it's quant-specific.

jia: I ran FP16 too — recall@1 was 0.725, so FP16 is fine. Strong indicator quantization axis is the culprit.

sam: Also sanity-check the FAISS metric — was it cosine or inner product? If embeddings were whitened but index uses L2, numbers will move.
jia: Index used inner product (we normalized embeddings). Verified metric alignment.

karen: Next steps proposal: 
- run 3 calibration variants (wiki1000, short-query, combined)
- per-channel symmetric vs per-channel asymmetric
- run small K=1/5/10 recall + local UMAP and silhouette

emily: If you want I can spin up the broader eval (longer holdout + multilang) — will take ~3h on staging.

jia: That would be great — can you kick it off? Job config in S3: s3://redwood-evals/jobs/spectra-v2/smoke-config.json

ops-bot: Submitted job spectra-v2-eval-2026-03-21-01 to staging cluster (job id: job-87321). Logs: https://staging-logs/redwood/job-87321

ben: If staging shows same pattern, we should try asymmetric quant + an extra per-channel clamp step (clip outliers) — I’ll open a tiny PR to add clamp flag to quantizer.

jia: Thanks all — I’ll update here with the staging results + UMAP screenshots. :eyes:
